answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Like a jetty holding back the tide, a small stake plus a record of attested work lets honest agents earn trust gradually: new identities transact only in small amounts, and their limits rise only after established peers endorse their work. Copies cost the same stake and time as the original, so flooding the network brings no profit. Water seeps through karst slowly; likewise, reputation should accumulate slowly, while bad behavior is exposed fast and washed away.
